HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Low three-quarter close two-shot inside a Goguryeo house at night, timber posts, a faded painting of the birth goddess on the wall dissolving into bokeh. YEON'S WIFE lies back against bolsters, hair undone, damp with sweat, smiling a tired private smile at the NEWBORN on her chest, swaddled in plain white cotton with a narrow band of brick-red #c25a4e silk at the edge of the wrap. YEON GESOMUN, a huge young Goguryeo commander still in his riding coat, kneels beside them, crown of his head bent low, one enormous scarred hand resting very lightly on the swaddle, his usually fierce face gone quiet and careful. One oil lamp on the floor at the right rakes across the white swaddle, her cheek and his knuckles; brick-red #c25a4e only in the silk band and the lamp's warm spill, not a glow. Foreground: a blurred lamp rim. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = gesomun, SECOND face = yeonwife. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. YEON GESOMUN — Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Colour #d0362f. YEONWIFE — Look: Composed Goguryeo noblewoman in her thirties: black hair braided and coiled up with a cluster of red silk flowers at the crown, loose strands at the cheeks, calm narrow eyes, small red mouth. Dress: Cut after the tomb owner's wife in the Ssangyeongchong mural: a long wide-sleeved jacket to the hip, crossed left over right and belted, in cream-buff silk with a broad rust-red band (襈) at the collar, cuffs and hem, over a long full skirt to the floor; a rust-red shawl over the arms, a long black sash. Jewelry: Goguryeo gold earrings: a thick hollow gold ring at each lobe with a short chain and a single heart-shaped gold leaf; no necklace, no bracelets. Colour #c4787a. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
